caption: Dermoids may be mostly cystic with linear floating echoes (dot and dash sign), consistent with hair . The echogenic shadowing Rokitansky nodule along the periphery is diagnostic for a dermoid.
Cystic lesion with echogenic fat-containing Rokitansky nodule is characteristic for mature cystic teratoma. These lesions can contain tissue from all 3 lines of embryonic cellular differentiation.
Fat-fluid level is seen in this mature cystic teratoma. As shown here, sometimes, a graded appearance can be seen with variable density of the fat contents.
On endovaginal imaging, layering fat with fat-fluid level is seen in the lesion. The level may not appear horizontal on endovaginal imaging.

Echogenic fat-containing lesion is consistent with a dermoid (calipers). Posterior acoustic enhancement can be seen from cystic contents of the lesion. Shadowing from certain areas of the mass precludes evaluation of deeper structures.

Color Doppler imaging usually does not demonstrate flow in the internal contents of dermoid. When flow is present, further evaluation with CECT or MR imaging should be considered to evaluate for possible malignant transformation.
CECT shows a lesion with fat density components . Calcified tooth-like structure is characteristic of a mature teratoma or dermoid.

Heterogeneous mixed solid-cystic mass is seen with echogenic areas , suggestive of dermoid. No flow is seen in the solid areas. However, given the heterogeneity, an MR was considered for definitive characterization.
Multiple locules of the mass demonstrate T2-hyperintense signal. The solid component demonstrates T2-hyperintense as well as intermediate-signal areas.
On fat-suppressed images, almost the entire mass, including both the cystic and solid areas, became hypointense, confirming the presence of macroscopic fat in a mature cystic teratoma.

caption: Macroscopic, fat-containing, mature cystic teratoma is seen. A calcified structure suggestive of teeth is seen.
Transabdominal ultrasound shows the echogenic component due to fat content.
Transverse CECT shows fat and calcium in a dermoid posterior to the uterus .
Transverse CECT shows more complex internal architecture in the fatty component as well as a solid portion anteriorly.

Transverse CECT shows edema of intraperitoneal fat adjacent to the mature cystic teratoma. The patient presented with acute abdominal pain. Torsion, suggested because of the edema, was confirmed surgically.
Transverse transvaginal ultrasound in a more easily recognizable case shows an echogenic mass arising from the left ovary , typical of mature cystic teratoma.
Transverse NECT shows a thick-walled mass with surrounding inflammatory change posterior to the bladder. Some fat and small flecks of calcification are noted within the mass.

Transverse transvaginal ultrasound shows an echogenic plug and a more cystic component . The patient presented with acute pain, and there was no demonstrable flow in the walls of the mass. Torsion of a teratoma was diagnosed at surgery.
Longitudinal transabdominal ultrasound shows a mass containing linear echoes superior to the uterus . Linear echoes are created by hair in mature cystic teratoma.
Corresponding transverse transvaginal ultrasound shows the echogenic fatty component to better advantage than the transabdominal scan. Again, note the linear echoes from hair.
Transverse T1WI MR shows a high-signal, right adnexal mass . The uterus is not well evaluated on this sequence.
Transverse T1WI MR with fat saturation in the same case shows loss of signal in the mass , confirming fat content. This is typical of a mature cystic teratoma.
Transverse T2WI MR in the same patient as the prior 2 images shows high signal in the mass as well as the normal internal architecture of the uterus and cervix .
On T1WI MR, dermoids have internal high signal that is consistent with fat .

Axial CECT of the same dermoid shows the calcified tooth , which is present in about 1/3 of cases. Notice that the fat within the dermoid is markedly hypodense compared to normal extraperitoneal fat .

Axial CECT in the same patient shows the layering areas of fat density in the left ovarian dermoid . A smaller dermoid is also present in the right ovary . 10-20% of dermoids are bilateral. Note the intrauterine device in the uterus.
Gross pathology shows the typical appearance of a Rokitansky nodule within the dissected mature cystic teratoma. Hair arises from the nodule.
Gross pathology shows the resected specimen with twisted vascular pedicle , solid nodule , and tangled hair .
Gross pathology shows fat within a mature cystic teratoma. Fat is liquid at body temperature but semisolid at room temperature.
